title: The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
lede: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO, but investigators still want to know what the company knew about Megaspeed, a Singapore customer accused of diverting its GPUs to China.

points: The US opened a Megaspeed investigation in 2024 and Singapore followed in 2025; Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.
Export lawyers say sellers rely on customer assurances but cannot ignore signs those assurances are unreliable, which is why Huang's affair with a Megaspeed executive matters.
On Monday the US restricted trade with Megaspeed and its affiliates; Nvidia said it will stop selling licensed chips to China and hire its first compliance officer.
Attorney General Todd Blanche suggested Nvidia is not a target, but California's AG and reportedly the SEC are probing its disclosures.
Three House committees will privately interview Huang and general counsel Tim Teter, and the Senate Banking Committee holds a public hearing on December 3.

sections.text: The case tests how far export-control liability reaches when a GPU vendor had reason to doubt a customer. New US rules also bar large data centers that buy US chips from serving customers in China.
